item.title: Daily News Brief — Oct 30, 2026: Binance loses $6.3 billion in record hack as issuers freeze stablecoins
item.description:
Friday edition covering Thursday, October 29 through Friday morning, October 30, 2026. Binance says about $6.3 billion was taken from its hot wallets in the largest crypto theft on record, apparently through an EIP-7702 delegation signed via a compromised engineer's laptop, and about $3 billion has been frozen, including more than $1.5 billion of USDT by Tether, about $823 million of USDC by Circle and about $200 million of RLUSD by Ripple, which makes it the largest live test yet of stablecoin freeze powers and DeFi circuit breakers. The Bank of England consults on supervisory expectations for CCPs accepting tokenised collateral, saying the current framework is no barrier if the collateral can be valued, transferred and realised under stress. ICE signs a definitive agreement with Trade[XYZ] to bring Hyperliquid-style perpetual futures onshore with a new retail clearing structure, and OKX ICE stock-token objections reach 38 with Walmart and Eli Lilly, while Canton-based TSV says the first trade under the SEC innovation exemption could come Monday. Also: Chainlink 24/7 pricing for tokenized assets with Aave as first adopter, the CPMI's report on the role of central bank money, Galaxy's OCC trust bank application, DTCC's 2027 roadmap to Stellar and Arc, and Coinbase's MiCA stablecoin conversion.

item.title: Daily News Brief — Oct 29, 2026: DTCC Tokenization Service goes live with 20 firms and 34 securities
item.description:
Thursday edition covering Wednesday, October 28 through Thursday morning, October 29, 2026. DTCC switches on the DTCC Tokenization Service on Canton and its private Besu network, with twenty signed DTC participants including JP Morgan, Citi, Bank of America and Fidelity, but only thirty-four eligible securities at launch, a business-day cross-chain conversion window, no built-in cash leg yet, and BNY and Goldman absent from the list. Objections to the OKX ICE tokenized stock venue reach thirty-three, with JP Morgan, Coca-Cola and Dell opting out, as Robinhood Chain adds eight stock tokens and DeFi lending against stock tokens exposes weekend gap risk. Visa's stablecoin settlement run rate passes $25 billion and RLUSD lands on Coinbase. Also: Circle asks the SEC to treat compliant stablecoins as cash with a zero haircut, the CFTC sets a December 15 roundtable on 24/7 trading, Hong Kong's IFEC warns on secondary trading of tokenized funds, the Fed holds with two hawkish dissents, Google previews institutional MPC custody, Securitize adds Stellar, Pontoro launches a liquidity pool for private assets, and Chainlink brings S&P vault risk assessments on chain.

item.title: Daily News Brief — Oct 28, 2026: Ripple wires RLUSD into BNY and Robinhood as Moody's rates it A2
item.description:
Wednesday edition covering Tuesday, October 27 through Wednesday morning, October 28, 2026. On day one of Swell, Ripple wired RLUSD into BNY custody, with planned direct minting and redemption through the bank, and into Robinhood's treasury and settlement operations, while Moody's assigned RLUSD an A2 and P-1 deposit rating and flagged the remaining bankruptcy-remoteness gap. Janus Henderson and Centrifuge launched JQQQ, a Nasdaq-licensed tokenized Nasdaq-100 fund on Stellar, Ondo brought fifteen stock tokens to Robinhood Chain, and Vlad Tenev said the SEC's innovation exemption needs durable rules behind it. In Europe, ten trade associations warned that the market integration package could shut euro stablecoins out of settlement and collateral roles, as Coinbase drops fourteen non-MiCA stablecoins on Friday. Also: Lynq and ZeroBeta put tokenized Treasuries to work as yield-bearing margin on Avalanche, Chainlink's CustodySync with Anchorage, Bessent at Swell, Circle's Arc passing $1 billion in USDC, Ethereum's Glamsterdam deposit fix, and what to watch on DTCC's tokenization service go-live.
Sources: Ripple, BNY explore using the XRP Ledger to finance approved invoices (The Block) — item.title: Daily News Brief — Oct 27, 2026: Ripple wins final OCC trust bank charter
item.description:
Tuesday edition covering Monday, October 26 through Tuesday morning, October 27, 2026. Ripple wins final OCC approval for Ripple National Trust Bank, bringing RLUSD reserves under federal supervision ahead of GENIUS Act rules. Hong Kong's SFC approves the first 24/7 secondary trading of publicly offered tokenized money market funds, and issuer objections to the OKX ICE tokenized stock venue reach 26 with IBM, Oracle, Intel and IonQ. Canada publishes draft stablecoin regulations with a yield ban, three-day redemption and a 1% fee cap. item.title: Daily News Brief — Oct 26, 2026: Issuer objections to OKX ICE stock tokens hit 22

Weekend edition covering Friday, October 23 through Monday morning, October 26, 2026. Objections to the OKX ICE tokenized stock venue climb to 22 of 62 issuers, including Wells Fargo, Cisco and Arm, as a Wall Street Journal ad warns CEOs against stock tokenization. Hyperliquid opens eleven offshore share-backed equity tokens from EQX Labs, and OpenWorld's Blockchain Common Stock on Figure OPEN stays on track for Q4 — two direct challenges to the DTC-centered settlement model. Stablecoin supply falls to about $300 billion and tokenized Treasuries shrink, while Anchorpoint slows its Hong Kong dollar stablecoin retail launch. item.title: Daily News Brief — Oct 23, 2026: OCC finalizes GENIUS Act rule; JPM Coin comes to Ethereum
item.description:
Week in review for October 19–23, 2026, and the first episode with the new digital cash segment. The OCC finalizes its GENIUS Act stablecoin rule with looser liquidity, reserve and yield terms; JPMorgan brings JPM Coin to Ethereum mainnet; the SEC names tokenization in its fiscal 2027 exam priorities; and sixteen issuers object to their stock trading on OKX ICE. Also: the DTC Tokenization Service details, BlackRock's push for tokenized money funds as collateral, ESMA's tokenised collateral call for evidence, HSBC RedCoin, SoFi's tokenized deposit, and BLOOM's expansion.
